source: FishMIP (Fisheries and Marine Ecosystem Model Intercomparison Project), ISIMIP3b simulation round, sector marine-fishery_global, via the ISIMIP Repository (data.isimip.org)
citation: Tittensor, D.P. et al. (2021) Next-generation ensemble projections reveal higher climate risks for marine ecosystems. Nature Climate Change 11, 973-981. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-021-01173-9. Model outputs from the FishMIP modelling groups (APECOSM, BOATS, DBPM, EcoOcean, FEISTY, ZooMSS), the ISIMIP sector coordinators and the ISIMIP cross-sectoral science team.
licence: CC0 1.0 (ISIMIP Repository rights field for every file used)
variable_meaning: Total consumer biomass: the weight of all animals each model represents (fish, and in some models invertebrates), per square metre of sea. Models count different sets of animals, so only % change within a model is meaningful.
fishing: No fishing ('nat' runs), as in Tittensor et al. 2021: climate is the only pressure, so this is what the ocean could support, not what will be caught.
weighting: Equal weight per run (one run = one ecosystem model x one Earth-system model). Models run with both Earth-system models count twice; 6 of 10 runs use IPSL.
range_rule: lo/hi are the 10th and 90th percentiles (linear interpolation) when n >= 10, otherwise the minimum and maximum of the runs.
method_note: For each run, biomass is averaged over each period cell by cell, then over the zone with each 1-degree cell weighted by its area (proportional to cos latitude), using cells whose centres fall inside the zone. % change = future mean / 1995–2014 mean − 1. 'median', 'lo', 'hi' summarise the runs that cover the zone ('n'); 'agree' is the share of those runs with the same sign as the median; 'by_run' lists each run's value in the order of 'runs' (null = that model has no ocean there). 'approx': the zone is too small to contain a cell centre, so the nearest ocean cells (within 0.75°, else 1.5°, else 3°) stand in. Countries pool the cells of their home zones ('zones' lists them; overseas territories keep their own entries); the world pools every ocean cell including the high seas and also gives the ensemble 'mean', the statistic FishMIP papers report.

world_check.definition: Ensemble mean (sd) of the same runs, 2090–2099 vs 1990–1999, the window used by Tittensor et al. 2021

tittensor_2021_cmip6.note: ≈ values in the text, 9 models / 16 runs, of which ISIMIP now publishes tcb for 6 models / 10 runs

lotze_2019_cmip5.note: the previous (CMIP5) FishMIP ensemble, Lotze et al. 2019 PNAS, by 2100, ±4 and ±11 sd

zones: Spain (mainland, Med and Gulf of Cadiz)
